text: The National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) is dedicated to maintain a secure, reliable and user-friendly registration system for the citizens of Pakistan. For this purpose, registration policy has been framed and it is updated from time to time. In this document, Birth certificate has been made the primary or breeder document for fresh / new registration in NADRA and in future any change in identity document, will only be made on the basis of prior correction in Birth certificate (if birth record exists in CRMS / NADRA record). Policy document has been outlined by considering the various sections of Pakistan Citizenship Act 1951 and NADRA Ordinance 2000 and its relevant rules and regulations.

This policy applies to all processes related to the new registration, renewal, change and attestation of identity documents for citizens of Pakistan, whether applying from inland or abroad. Moreover, it also covers all the manners of submission of application by applicant i.e., NADRA registration center (Inland / Abroad), Mobile units, Pak ID (DAU and Mobile App) etc. One document for all platforms. It encompasses all segments of society, including provisions for handling exceptional cases.

This policy also includes guidelines for processing applications for orphans, transgender, organ donors and exceptions. Exceptional cases will be referred to Regional DG/Director through DAU and Zonal board recommendations for approval.

• Regular training of staff on policy and its compliance is mandatory. • Strict enforcement of policy by all and with penalties for non-compliance be ensured. • Periodic reviews and updates to the policy will be carried out.

Various acronyms used in this document are listed below along with their full form: - ACC: Afghan Citizen Card MOI: Ministry of Interior BC: Birth Certificate NICOP: National Identity Card for Overseas Pakistani CBRC: Computerized Birth Registration Certificate NOC: No objection Certificate CD: Cancellation due to death OIC: Officer In-charge CNIC: Computerized National Identity Card OWC: One Window Counter CNICF: Computerized National Identity Card Form PO: Proclaimed Offender CRC: Child Registration Certificate POC: Pakistan Origin Card CRMS: Civil Registration Management System POR: Proof of Registration DAU: Data Acquisition Unit PRC: Permanent Residence Card DG: Director General QC: Quality Control DOB: Date of Birth RP: Registration Policy FRC: Family Registration Certificate RHO: Regional Head Office HOD: Head of Department SNIC: SMART National Identity Card ID: Identity Document SNICOP: SMART National Identity Card for Overseas Pakistani IMPASS: Immigration and Passport SOP: Standard Operating Procedure IOOD: International and Online Operation Department SPOC: SMART Pakistan Origin Card KSA: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia TID: Tracking ID MC: Marriage Certificate UC: Union Council MNIC: Manual National Identity Card UV: Under Verification

Terms Definition Applicant: An individual applying for the NADRA’s registration services Application: A request submitted to NADRA through any platform i.e. DAU, Mobile App etc. Biometrics Personal data resulting from specific technical processing relating to the physical, physiological or behavioral characteristics of a person which allow or confirm the unique identification of that person such as facial images or dactyloscopy data Biometric verification: Verification carried out under regulation 9 by parents or blood relatives during processing of an individual Breeder document: Primary document used to establish identity, such as a birth certificate or passport Cancellation: The permanent invalidation of a card or its associated data rendering it unusable for any purpose in accordance with the law Certificate: Any document in the physical or digital form issued by the Authority under the NADRA (NIC) Rules, 2002 Citizen: A person who is or is deemed to be a citizen of Pakistan, under the Pakistan Citizenship Act, 1951 Citizenship by birth: As per Section 4 of Pakistan Citizenship Act 1951 Citizenship by descent: As Per Section 5 of Pakistan Citizenship Act 1951 Civil card: Identity card issued by the foreign government Digitally impounded: Identity document marked digitally impounded under Section 18 of NADRA Ordinance Digitally marked: “Digitally Marked” means the process of embedding identifiable and traceable metadata in the Citizen Database for further verification. The term is used as an alternative of “UV”. Family: An alpha, beta or gamma family of a registered person Foreign detailed birth certificate: A document issued by concerned authority of a foreign country having minor and both parents’ information Guardianship certificate: A certificate issued by the court for the custody of minor Juvenile card: Identity Certificate in the form of card issued to minors (under 18) Manual birth certificate: Birth certificate issued before computerization of system Minor: A citizen under 18 years of age as per NADRA Ordinance 2000 Naturalization Certificate: A certificate granted under Pakistan Citizenship Act 1951 Non-Resident citizen: If a citizen is an emigrant or intending emigrant or intending to be resident abroad or holds resident visa or permit or status Regulations: Regulations made under Section 45 of NADRA Ordinance Renunciation certificate: A certificate issued by IMPASS upon surrender of Pakistani nationality Residence permit: Permission granted by the foreign government to an individual for legal stay in that country Resident citizen: A citizen shall be resident citizen if he is not a non-resident citizen RGI, RGII, RGIII: Old registration forms used for new registration, B-form and control register respectively Rules: Rules made under Section 44 of NADRA Ordinance Schedule: Attachment or appendix to a legal document S1 Form: Abroad birth registration form of minor issued by Pakistani Embassy / Consulate / Mission System independent: An individual having no blood relative (Father / Mother / Brother / Sister) Verification Board: Board constituted at Regional or Zonal level for under verification cases and determination of citizen's correct credentials

FRESH / NEW REGISTRATION

Registration under 18 (Minor) citizens: New / Fresh registration of under 18 years citizen is carried out under Section 9 of NADRA Ordinance 2000, wherein every parent or guardian is bound to register the minor within one month of his/her birth. Child Registration Certificate: Under this Registration, minor is issued an ID number on a certificate as per schedule VI under Rule 18 (1) of NIC Rules 2002 called Child registration certificate. Same number will be later used to obtain identity card on attaining the age of 18 years by minor. After amendment in NIC Rules 2002, CRC is issued to each child separately with biometrics information and expiry dates. Accordingly, presence of minors above age of three (03) years is mandatory. Additionally, photograph of minors below the age of three (03) years shall also be captured for the purpose of passport issuance. Juvenile card: This is also a certificate issued to a citizen of below 18 years under Rule 18(1) in the form of a card, carrying same value as of CRC. However, while registering through this certificate, minor has to be present as a primary applicant.

Applicable to all types of Fresh / New registration of below and above 18 years of age mentioned above I. Applicant can apply from anywhere in Pakistan/abroad. II. All applicants shall be processed through Digitally Marking (UV) checklist. III. OIC shall interview each applicant / parent and verifier / witness using available tools and information provided by applicant. Evaluate through cross questioning and mention findings, recommendations and observations at interview / approval stage. Applicant shall not be denied for processing and any exception on above mentioned requirements must be communicated to the applicant for provision of relevant documents. IV. If any one of the parents is registered with NADRA and his/her card is not digitally impounded, then children of such parents be registered without any hindrance. (Ref: MOI letter no 8/37/2016-NADRA of 6 June 2018). Cogent reason must be mentioned for marking record as Digitally Marked (UV) i.e. contradiction in family information etc. Family of proclaimed offender (PO) may also be processed without any hindrance. V. If D.O.B. of applicant (parent not ID holder) is after the commencement of Citizenship Act 13 April, 1951 and place of birth is not Pakistan OR D.O.B. of applicant is after 16 December 1971 and place of birth is Bangladesh, record shall be handled through Digitally Marking (UV) procedure. VI. Particulars of applicant should be as per Birth certificate. In case of Non-resident, foreign passport information will be preferred. VII. For marital status as married / divorced / widow, documentary requirement as per relevant standard will be applicable. VIII. Temporary and permanent address will be applicable as per relevant standard. IX. In case of unknown parentage, parents’ name will be randomly selected by system (For Orphans and transgender persons only). Necessary affidavit(s) as per specimen along with primary requirement shall be fulfilled. In Orphan, adoption and transgender cases where parents are unknown, CBRC is not mandatory. X. For Disability logo, certificate issued by CRPD (Council on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities) / PCRDP (Provincial Council for Rehabilitation of Disabled Persons) / Social welfare AJK / GB / Foreign institute will be required. Disability certificate is mandatory for Illiterate applicant having Hearing & Intellectual impairment (where interview not possible). XI. For Organ Donor logo, certificate / card issued by BINUQ (Balochistan Institute of Nephro-Urology Quetta), HOTA (Human Organ Transplant Authority Islamabad), PHOTA (Punjab Human Organ Transplant Authority), KPMTERA (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Medical Transplantation Regulatory Authority) or Government Hospitals of Sindh will be required. XII. Case of Indian held Kashmiri (IHK), holding State Subject certificate, will be processed after verification from issuing authority; attestation will be carried out as per attestation standard. XIII. Naturalization/Citizenship certificate shall be verified from IMPASS. XIV. Guardian is authorized to process through guardianship certificate issued by court of competent jurisdiction. XV. Approval be sought from Regional DG for any other exception(s) after evaluation and interview of case at Zonal or Regional Board. XVI. Preference of Biometric verification shall be given to parent(s). If parents are not alive / available then verification from sibling(s) will be carried out. If both parents or siblings are not alive / available then attestation of Application Form shall be required as per Regulation 9 (a-h). In such cases, child cannot be declared as head of the family. Reason of non-availability of parents or siblings should be mentioned at approval stage. XVII. Spouse and children shall not be verifier in fresh cases (Above 18 years of age). XVIII. Birth proof for Ex-POC (less foreign spouse) will be optional for CNIC / NICOP processing. XIX. Fresh NICOP applications from KSA having late registration, expired parents’ or siblings’ ID cards and holding manual passports issued from Jeddah will be referred to Pak Mission Jeddah for verification. The marking of CD is mandatory in NADRA record. XX. If applicant’s (Non-resident citizen) age is less than 10 years and has provided S-1 form or Foreign Birth certificate, then passport or any other document is optional. XXI. Original document must be seen and scanned. However, NADRA’s issued documents (ID cards / Certificates / Vital Event Certificates) are not required to be scanned. Application form shall not be printed and scanned except cases where attestation is required under Regulation 9(a-h) of NADRA (Application for NIC) Regulations, 2002. XXII. Endorsement of child on Pakistani passport of parent is also acceptable as birth proof. XXIII. Religion of minors shall be recorded as per father’s religion in NADRA record. If father is not registered, then religion will be mentioned as per mother’s religion in NADRA record. XXIV. For SI cases, OIC shall check documents, ascertain genuineness of the SI claim through interview of applicant and witnesses, shall record remarks at approval stage. All SI cases shall be finally decided (cleared / permanent rejected) by the DG RHO concerned through NFC Portal. The final decision shall be recorded with brief decision. XXV. Cases of applicants who previously registered on the basis of witness (as SI) by selecting option: • “None of the blood relative is alive”, shall not be processed for addition of parents and siblings in future. • “Applicant’s blood relatives (Father/Mother/Brother/Sister) are unregistered, untraceable or not available”, parents / siblings shall only be added in future upon provision of justified reasons and rigorous verification / confirmation through Zonal Verification Board. POC

Background: POC is issued under Section 11 of NADRA Ordinance 2000 and Rules 3, 4, 5,9 and 10 of POC Rules 2002. The scheme of POC was conceived and launched by Government of Pakistan as a result of repeated requests and resolutions of Overseas Pakistanis Conventions held during November 1997 and August 1999 under the auspices of Overseas Pakistanis Foundations, Ministry of Labor, Manpower and Overseas Pakistanis. This Scheme for issuance of Pakistan Origin Card to eligible Foreigner of Pakistan origin was launched in 2002. POC is renewed as per Rule 15, whereas duplicate and changes in card are made under Rule 16 of POC rules 2002.

Following are benefits of POC which can be availed by a POC holder till the validity of the card: a. May enter Pakistan without a visa from such port or place, by such route and in accordance with such conditions, if any, as are prescribed for citizens of Pakistan under section 13 of the Passport Act, 1974 (XX of 1974). b. Shall have permission to stay in Pakistan till the validity of the card. c. Shall, during their stay in Pakistan, be exempt as a Foreigner from reporting to, or registering with, any law enforcing or other governmental agency with which such report or registration in the capacity of a Foreigner is otherwise required under any law in force in Pakistan. d. May open bank accounts anywhere in Pakistan and transact business therein subject to fulfillment of the requirements of any other law for the time being in force. e. May, subject to any other law for the time being in force, enter into transaction of purchase and sale of movable or immovable property anywhere in Pakistan and deal with and dispose of such property. f. May use the card for establishing and proving his / her identity anywhere in Pakistan where a National Identity Card is required for the purpose. g. May obtain an employment.
